Ava (Finance Ops): :loudspeaker: Temporary p-card policy in effect. Effective immediately were applying a $5,000/month cap per corporate card to limit exposure after recent anomalous vendor activity. This will be reviewed and is currently planned through 2026-04-15.

Ava (Finance Ops): Practical impact: any single charge that would push a card past $5k in a calendar month will be declined. If you have planned essential spend above that threshold, submit an exception via the procurement-exception form (link below). Exceptions require FP&A + Procurement approval and are reserved for business-critical items.

Ava (Finance Ops): Links: Confluence FAQ https://redwood.internal/confluence/pcard-temp-cap; Exception form https://redwood.internal/forms/procurement-exception. For live-incident vendor payments put "INCIDENT" in the subject and tag @Sam.

Diego (FP&A): Teams, please audit vendor commitments for the next 30 days and notify FP&A of re-prioritized items by EOD tomorrow. We'll triage against Q2 forecasts.

Lina (Eng Manager): Q: pre-approved Dedicated infra burst credits are they impacted?

Sam (Procurement): If spend is under an existing contract or approved burst credit, its grandfathered. The cap applies to new single-card charges only. If autoscaling could push you over, file an exception and cc procurement@redwood.com with the contract reference.

Lina (Eng Manager): Thanks, will file.

Diego (FP&A): Exceptions will be reviewed by FP&A + Procurement + Finance Ops with a 24-48h target. Mark "EXPEDITE" for customer-impacting requests.

Accounting Bot: Automated: reconciliation cadence unchanged; attach receipts in Concur within 5 business days to avoid holds.

Ava (Finance Ops): Sorry for the temporary friction. This reduces risk while we complete the vendor activity review. DM me for urgent edge cases. :pray:
